claim: Resveratrol supplementation improves cardiovascular or metabolic health outcomes in humans

rows.integrity_note: RETRACTED (Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol 2012;302(11):H2446, DOI 10.1152/ajpheart.zh4-0450-retr.2012; retraction PMID:22833916). PubMed article-type 'Retracted Publication'. Isolated rat-heart study from the Dipak K. Das lab (UConn Cardiovascular Research Center); retracted amid UConn's misconduct finding of data fabrication/falsification across Das's lab. Animal, not human, and fraudulent — excluding it removes the mechanistic 'cardioprotection' anchor.
rows.finding: Claimed resveratrol pharmacologically preconditions/protects the ischemic rat heart via NO. Data from the retracted study; not usable as evidence.

rows.integrity_note: Sahebkar 2013, Nutr Rev (DOI 10.1111/nure.12081). 7 RCTs, n=282 (141 per arm). Independent of any Das work.
rows.finding: No significant effect of resveratrol on total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, or triglycerides; robust to dose, duration, and CV-risk status. Null surrogate outcomes.

rows.integrity_note: Sahebkar/Banach 2015, Int J Cardiol (DOI 10.1016/j.ijcard.2015.04.008). 10 RCTs / 11 treatment arms.
rows.finding: No benefit on CRP, total cholesterol, LDL, triglycerides, glucose, or systolic/diastolic BP; slightly lowered HDL. Concludes no benefit on CV risk factors. Surrogate endpoints only.

rows.integrity_note: Akbari/Asemi 2019, High Blood Press Cardiovasc Prev (DOI 10.1007/s40292-019-00324-6). 28 RCTs (33 findings). Very high heterogeneity (I2=96.5%) undercuts reliability.
rows.finding: Significantly increased flow-mediated dilation (surrogate) in metabolic syndrome, but no effect on systolic or diastolic BP. Mixed/surrogate-only; heterogeneity extreme.

rows.integrity_note: Gimblet/Jalal 2024, CJASN (DOI 10.2215/CJN.0000000000000337). NCT03597568. Small (n=28), 6-week crossover, single surrogate endpoint.
rows.finding: 400 mg/d resveratrol improved brachial-artery flow-mediated dilation vs placebo in CKD+diabetes; no change in eGFR, HbA1c, BP. Positive but surrogate-only, tiny, short.

rows.integrity_note: Zortea 2016, Nutrients (DOI 10.3390/nu8020073). NCT02062190. Very small (n=19 men), 4 weeks.
rows.finding: 200 mg/d resveratrol produced no significant change in body weight, waist circumference, glucose, or total cholesterol in schizophrenia patients. Null.

rows.integrity_note: Faghihzadeh 2015, Br J Nutr (DOI 10.1017/S0007114515002433). n=50, 12 weeks, NAFLD.
rows.finding: 500 mg/d resveratrol gave no significant change in blood pressure, insulin-resistance markers, lipid profile, or anthropometrics (reduced ALT/steatosis only). Null on CV/metabolic risk factors.

rows.integrity_note: Saldanha/Mafra 2016, J Ren Nutr (DOI 10.1053/j.jrn.2016.06.005). Pilot, n=20, 4-week crossover.
rows.finding: 500 mg/d resveratrol had no antioxidant/anti-inflammatory effect (Nrf2, NF-kB, cytokines unchanged) in non-dialyzed CKD patients. Null.

integrity_records.study: Hattori R, Otani H, Maulik N, Das DK. Pharmacological preconditioning with resveratrol: role of nitric oxide. Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol. 2002;282(6):H1988-95. PMID:12003802 / DOI:10.1152/ajpheart.01012.2001
integrity_records.wording: RETRACTED. PubMed article-type 'Retracted Publication'. Formal retraction notice: 'Retraction. Pharmacological preconditioning with resveratrol: role of nitric oxide.' Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol 2012;302(11):H2446 (PMID:22833916; DOI:10.1152/ajpheart.zh4-0450-retr.2012), published June 1, 2012. Retracted following the University of Connecticut Health Center's investigation of Dipak K. Das, which found data fabrication/falsification across his Cardiovascular Research Center lab and led to ~20 retractions. This paper is a rat-heart (non-human) study and cannot support a human-outcomes claim.

integrity_records.study: Dipak K. Das research-misconduct case (University of Connecticut Health Center investigation, 2012)
integrity_records.wording: UConn reported a three-year, ~60,000-page investigation finding 145 counts of fabrication and falsification of data across Dipak K. Das's Cardiovascular Research Center lab; 11 journals were notified and the university declined federal grant funds. Das's body of work underpinned many resveratrol-cardioprotection claims. Reported by Retraction Watch (June 4, 2012).
